JX 行李異常案件分析報告JX Baggage Mishandling Case Analysis Report

全場站行李營運總覽：延誤/遺失與破損案件、跨航理賠分攤、超重行李、艙等裝載、自助行李託運與旅客真實起訖。金額依公司官方月匯率換算台幣。資料涵蓋 2026 年 1–7 月（七個完整月份）。本版全部區塊皆隨上方篩選器即時重算——月份、類型、場站三個條件會同時作用；唯第 06–11 區逐月趨勢刻意固定顯示全部七個月（趨勢需完整期間才有意義）。Network-wide baggage operations overview: delayed / missing and damaged cases, interline baggage claim proration, excess baggage, baggage loading by cabin class, self bag drop and true passenger origin & destination. 3 分鐘營運執行摘要3-Minute Operations Executive Summary

供運務處主管會議快速掌握：全場站現況、最需關注場站、本期財務風險。以下為 2026 年 1–7 月全期值，不隨篩選器變動。A quick read for the Airport Operations Div. management meeting: network status, the stations needing most attention, and financial risk this period. The figures below cover the full Jan–Jul 2026 period and do not change with the filters.

① 全場站現況① Network Status

  • 七個月案件 8,576 件、已付賠償 794.1 萬元；異常結構破損主導：破損 76.6%、失竊 0.3%、延誤 23.1%，與全球「延誤主導」（破損僅 18%）相反。8,576 cases and TWD 7.94M of compensation paid over seven months; the mishandling mix is damage-dominated: Damaged 76.6%, Pilfered 0.3%, Delayed 23.1% — the reverse of the global "delay-dominated" pattern (damage only 18%).
  • JX 可控起程站率 2.19／千客（全案報案率 2.41），對比亞太基準 3.41；惟延誤案恐未完整入庫，不宜逕判優於業界。JX-controllable departure-station rate 2.19 per 1,000 pax (all-case reporting-station rate 2.41), against the Asia-Pacific benchmark of 3.41; but delayed cases may not be fully captured, so this cannot be read as outperforming the industry.
  • 異常率七個月持續下降（2.63→1.87，−28.9%），已排除航網組合與結案延遲兩種假象；但本期無對應改善專案，尚不可歸因為營運改善（見第 24 區洞察一）。The mishandled baggage rate fell for seven consecutive months (2.63→1.87, −28.9%), and both the network-mix and the closing-lag artefacts have been ruled out; but there was no corresponding improvement project this period, so it cannot yet be attributed to operational improvement (see Insight 1 in Section 24).

② 三個最需關注場站② Three Stations Needing Most Attention

  • 美國線（起程率）：SEA 10.17、LAX 9.40、SFO 6.48；五站占運量 6.0% 卻占 JX 可控案件 21.2%、率為全場站 3.5 倍。U.S. routes (departure-station rate): SEA 10.17, LAX 9.40, SFO 6.48; the five stations carry 6.0% of traffic but account for 21.2% of JX-controllable cases, a rate 3.5 times the network average.
  • TPE（絕對量）：起程案件 1,978 件最大（率僅 1.28）→ 母基地裝卸規模效應。TPE (absolute volume): the largest departure-station case count at 1,978 cases (rate only 1.28) → the scale effect of loading and unloading at the home base.
  • PHX／北美（時效）：PHX 結案 45.8 天、SFO 19.0、LAX 16.0 天 → 賠付授權鏈過慢。PHX / North America (Days to Close): PHX 45.8 days, SFO 19.0, LAX 16.0 days → the payout authorization chain is too slow.
  • ※ 主指標為起程站：報案站只是旅客發現地、非出事地。※ The primary metric is the Departure Station: the reporting station is only where the passenger noticed the problem, not where it happened.

③ 本期財務風險③ Financial Risk This Period

  • 另資料收集中 246 件 · US$6,862帳齡增長中，須搶在索賠期限前補件催收。A further 246 cases · US$6,862 still collecting documentation are ageing; documents must be completed and recovery pursued before the claim deadlines.

01

每千名旅客行李異常率Mishandled Baggage Rate per 1,000 Passengers

業界核心 KPI · 隨篩選器連動Industry core KPI · live with filters

重點KEY POINT主指標為起程站；與 SITA 全球 4.9／亞太 3.41 只能概念對照——分子是「案件數」而非「行李件數」，且延誤案可能未完整入庫，總率偏低不代表優於業界。The primary basis is the departure station; the comparison with SITA's global 4.9 and Asia-Pacific 3.41 is conceptual only — the numerator counts cases, not bags, and delayed cases may not be fully captured, so a lower overall rate cannot be read as outperforming the industry.

判讀須知（重要）：① 分子為「案件／報案數」非 SITA 的「行李件數」，故與 4.9 基準僅為概念對照。② 本資料（依 RL 代碼分類；KPI「破損占比」係以破損分頁計、含失竊案，兩者基準不同故有約 0.3 個百分點差），與全球「延誤主導」結構相反，因此總率偏低主要來自延誤率低，不代表整體優於業界。③ 分母為各站離站旅客數（P31 航段起點歸戶，逐月已與檔案合計列核對相符）。
④ WorldTracer 建單特性：本報告延誤案比重偏低，可能反映建單／結案特性；運務處應同步關注「未建單之現場個案」，避免真實延誤被低估。
⑤ 為何以「起程站」為主？旅客必然是抵達後才會發現行李沒到或破損，因此「報案站」只是發現地、不等於出事地，直接用報案站排名會誤指責任。故主欄改以起程站（行李進入 JX 掌控的第一站）歸戶，分子分母同為「該站出發的旅客」，口徑一致；報案站率保留為淺字對照。
⑥ 破損的地點歸屬：破損案件雖列入起程站（代表裝載端），但破損可能發生於裝載、運送或卸載任一環節，單站歸戶無法斷定責任；完整歸戶見第 02 區破損航段表。
⑦ 月份口徑：分子以建檔月歸戶（與 WorldTracer 月報一致）、分母必然是航班月，各月約 2.1–3.0% 的案件其航班發生於他月。因每月流入與流出量相近而互相抵銷，對趨勢方向無影響，僅影響單月絕對水準。How to read this (important): ① The numerator is "cases / reports filed", not SITA's "bags", so the comparison with the 4.9 benchmark is conceptual only. ② In this dataset (classified by RL code; the KPI "damaged share" is counted from the damage worksheet and includes pilferage cases, so the two bases differ by about 0.3 pp), the reverse of the global "delay-dominated" structure; the low overall rate therefore comes mainly from a low delay rate and does not mean the network outperforms the industry. ③ The denominator is departing passengers at each station (attributed to the P31 segment origin; reconciled month by month against the file's own total rows).
④ WorldTracer filing characteristics: the low share of delayed cases in this report may reflect filing and closing practice; Airport Operations Div. should also watch on-the-spot cases for which no file is raised, so that real delays are not understated.
⑤ Why is the Departure Station the primary basis? A passenger can only discover that a bag is missing or damaged after arrival, so the "reporting station" is only where it was found, not where it happened; ranking stations directly by reports filed would misassign responsibility. The main column therefore attributes cases to the Departure Station (the first station at which the bag came under JX control), so that numerator and denominator both refer to passengers departing that station; the reporting-station rate is kept in light type for comparison.
⑥ Where damage is attributed: damage cases are listed under the departure station (representing the loading end), but damage can occur at loading, in transit or at unloading, and single-station attribution cannot establish responsibility; for the full attribution see the damage-by-segment table in Section 02.
⑦ Month basis: the numerator is attributed by creation month (consistent with the WorldTracer monthly report) while the denominator is necessarily by flight month; in each month about 2.1–3.0% of cases relate to flights in another month. Inflows and outflows are similar in size each month and offset each other, so there is no effect on the direction of the trend — only on the absolute level of an individual month.

01

核心異常率走勢 · 移動平均 · 統計管制界線Core Mishandled Baggage Rate · Moving Average · Statistical Control Limits

用途：這是整份報告的主脈，回答「行李異常的整體水準往哪個方向走」。 藍線是每月的 JX 可控起程站異常率，褐色虛線是三個月移動平均（把單月雜訊抹平、看趨勢骨架）， 三條水平線分別是全期平均與 ±2 個標準差的管制界線。 意義：管制界線是製程管制圖的標準作法——落在界線內代表這是穩定的趨勢移動， 落在界線外才是需要事件回溯的突發異常。這比「某月比其他月均值高兩倍」的規則更早抓到緩慢惡化， 因為緩慢惡化永遠不會觸發兩倍規則。Purpose: This is the backbone of the entire report. It answers one question — which way is the overall level of mishandled baggage moving? The blue line is the monthly JX-controllable mishandled baggage rate on a departure station basis. The bronze dashed line is the three-month moving average, which smooths out single-month noise and shows the underlying trend. The three horizontal lines are the full-period average and the control limits at ±2 standard deviations. What it means: Control limits are standard practice in process control charts. A point inside the limits is ordinary trend movement. Only a point outside the limits is an exceptional event that warrants going back to find out what happened. This catches slow deterioration far earlier than a rule such as "this month is twice the average of the others," because slow deterioration never trips a doubling rule.

02

破損率走勢（每千件行李）Damage Rate Trend (/1,000 Bags)

用途：破損案占本網全部異常的四分之三，是總異常率的主要驅動力，因此值得單獨拉出來看。 分母用「行李件數」而非旅客數，因為破損是發生在行李上、不是發生在人身上。 意義：把它跟上一張並排看就能判斷——如果總異常率在降、破損率也在降，那是同一件事； 如果總異常率降但破損率持平，代表下降來自延誤側，成因完全不同。Purpose: Damaged bags account for three quarters of all mishandling on this network and are the main driver of the overall rate, so they are worth isolating. The denominator here is bags handled rather than passengers, because damage happens to a bag, not to a person. What it means: Read side by side with the previous chart. If the overall rate is falling and the damage rate is falling too, they are the same story. If the overall rate falls while the damage rate stays flat, the decline is coming from the delayed side, and the causes are entirely different.

03

賠償金額走勢與資料成熟度Compensation Trend and Data Maturity

用途：看賠付支出的月度變化。但這張圖有個必須先講清楚的陷阱： 賠償金額是在案件結案時才入帳，未結案的案件金額掛零。 意義：因此最近幾個月的金額必然被低估，空心圓點標示的就是結案率未達 95% 的月份。 末段的下滑不可以解讀為賠償減少——要看真實走勢請看件數與異常率，它們用建檔月歸戶、不受結案進度影響。Purpose: Tracks month-to-month compensation spend. But there is a trap that has to be stated first: compensation is booked only when a case is closed. Cases still open carry a value of zero. What it means: The most recent months are therefore necessarily understated. The hollow markers flag the months whose closure rate is below 95%. The fall at the right-hand end must not be read as compensation coming down. For the real trend, use case counts and the mishandled baggage rate — those are assigned by creation month and are unaffected by closing progress.

04

結構調整檢定：下降是真實的，還是航網組合造成的？Mix-Adjusted Test: Is the Decline Real, or an Effect of Network Mix?

用途：回答一個主管一定會問的問題——異常率下降，是「各站真的變好」， 還是「高風險航線的運量占比變小」造成的錯覺？作法是把各站的率固定用首月的運量權重重新加權， 如果組合效果是主因，調整後的線就會變平。 意義：兩條線幾乎重疊代表下降不是組合效果、是各站率普遍下移； 但「普遍下移」仍不等於「營運改善」，其他解釋（判定尺度改變、分母成長稀釋、季節性）尚未被排除， 待查證事項見洞察一。Purpose: Answers a question every executive will ask. The mishandled baggage rate is down — but is that because stations genuinely improved, or because higher-risk routes now carry a smaller share of traffic? The test re-weights every station's rate using the first month's traffic weights throughout. If mix is the main driver, the adjusted line flattens out. What it means: Two lines that almost overlap show the decline is not a mix effect — station-level rates moved down broadly. But a broad decline still does not equal operational improvement. Other explanations (a change in filing thresholds, dilution from denominator growth, seasonality) have not been ruled out. Items to be verified are listed in Insight 1.

07

異常結構拆解趨勢Mishandling Mix Breakdown Trends

結構是否改變 · 驗證下降的真偽Has the mix changed · testing whether the decline is real

重點KEY POINT破損占比上升、延誤占比下降，結構確實出現位移；但尚須釐清是真實變化，還是建單判定尺度改變。The damage share rose and the delay share fell, so the mix has genuinely shifted; whether this is a real change or a change in filing practice remains to be established.

05

異常類型結構逐月占比（破損／延誤／失竊）Monthly Mix by Mishandling Type (Damaged / Delayed / Pilfered)

用途：本網最大的結構特徵是「破損主導」（破損約 76%，全球基準只有 18%）。 這張圖看的是這個結構本身穩不穩定。 意義：這是驗證洞察一的關鍵圖。如果破損占比下降、延誤占比上升， 那總異常率的下降就更可能來自「破損建單判定尺度改變」而非品質改善—— 因為真正的品質改善不會讓兩類案件此消彼長。反之若三類占比穩定，就支持「整體水準真的在降」。Purpose: The defining structural feature of this network is that damage dominates — roughly 76% of cases, against an industry benchmark of 18%. This chart asks whether that structure itself is stable. What it means: This is the key chart for testing Insight 1. If the damaged share falls while the delayed share rises, the decline in the overall rate is more likely to come from a change in the threshold for filing damage cases than from a quality improvement — genuine quality improvement does not make two case types trade off against each other. If instead all three shares hold steady, that supports a genuine decline in the overall level.

06

延誤成因結構逐月占比Monthly Mix by Delay Cause

用途：把延誤案依 IATA 官方成因大類拆開看逐月消長：轉接他航、營運／設備／天候、 拿錯／安檢、未能裝載、裝卸錯誤等。 意義：不同成因對應完全不同的責任單位與改善手段。轉接類要對外談 SLA、營運類要查設備與配載、 安檢類要跟機場端協調。看占比而非件數，是為了排除總量變動的干擾—— 即使總延誤件數在降，某一類的占比上升仍代表那一塊在惡化。Purpose: Breaks delayed cases into the official IATA cause categories and tracks how each moves month by month: transfer mishandling; airport / customs / weather / space-weight restriction; ticketing error / bag switch / security / other; failure to load; loading error. What it means: Each cause points to a different owner and a different remedy. Transfer cases are an SLA conversation with partners. Operational cases mean checking equipment and load planning. Security cases require coordination with the airport. Shares are shown instead of counts to strip out the effect of changing volume — even when total delayed cases are falling, a rising share in one category still means that category is getting worse.

07

前六大 RL 代碼逐月件數Monthly Cases — Top Six RL Codes

用途：比大類更細一層，直接看六個最常出現的 IATA 代碼： 80 一般破損、54 未從他航收到行李、65 艙位／重量限制、64 設備故障、74 拿錯行李、53 轉接 MCT 不足。 意義：代碼層級是最早的預警訊號。某個代碼連續兩個月上升，通常比總量提前三到四週出現， 而且代碼直接對應到現場的具體情境，看到就知道要查什麼。3 月洛杉磯的設備故障暴衝在這張圖上會直接跳出來。Purpose: One level finer than the cause categories — the six most frequent IATA codes: 80 general damage, 54 bag not received from other carrier, 65 space / weight restriction, 64 equipment failure, 74 bag switch, 53 MCT not available on transfer. What it means: Code level gives the earliest warning. A code rising for two consecutive months typically shows up three to four weeks before the total does, and each code maps to a specific situation on the ground, so the moment it appears you know what to go and check. The March spike in equipment failures at Los Angeles stands out immediately on this chart.

08

責任分群趨勢Liability Segmentation Trends

誰的責任 · 對應不同改善手段Whose responsibility · each calls for a different remedy

重點KEY POINT他航責任線可與總量分開看——若總量下降而他航線未動，代表改善來自內部、對外談判尚未見效。The other-carrier line can be read separately from the total — if the total falls while that line does not, the improvement is internal and the negotiations with partners have yet to bite.

08

JX 可控 vs 他航責任 逐月件數JX-Controllable vs Other-Carrier Liability — Monthly Cases

用途：把案件分成「我們自己造成的」與「他航交接失敗造成的」（RL 54 未從他航收到行李、 RL 77 他航作業錯誤）兩條線。後者已從所有站別率中剔除，避免把他航的問題算在 JX 場站頭上。 意義：這兩塊的改善手段完全不同——前者靠內部 SOP 與裝載流程，後者只能靠對外談判與 SLA。 混在一起看會誤判努力方向：如果總量在降但他航那條沒動，代表內部有改善而對外談判還沒見效。Purpose: Splits cases into two lines — those we caused ourselves, and those caused by interline transfer failure (RL 54 bag not received from other carrier, RL 77 other-carrier handling error). The latter is excluded from every station rate so that another carrier's problem is not charged to a JX station. What it means: The two groups call for entirely different remedies. The first is a matter of internal SOPs and loading process. The second can only be addressed through negotiation and SLAs with partners. Reading them together misdirects effort: if the total is falling but the other-carrier line has not moved, internal work is paying off while the external negotiation has yet to bite.

09

美國五站 vs 其餘全場站 逐月異常率The Five U.S. Stations vs the Rest of the Network — Monthly Mishandled Baggage Rate

用途：美國五站（SEA／LAX／SFO／PHX／ONT）只占全場站運量 6%，卻占 JX 可控案件的兩成以上， 率是全場站的三倍多。這張圖追蹤這個差距是在收斂還是擴大。 意義：這是「以美國線起程站為單位重整收運與配載決策」這項措施的成效追蹤指標。 兩條線的距離縮小才代表措施有效；如果兩條線一起下降，那只是全場站共同因素、不是美國線的改善。Purpose: The five U.S. stations (SEA / LAX / SFO / PHX / ONT) carry only 6% of network traffic yet account for more than a fifth of JX-controllable cases, at a rate over three times the network average. This chart tracks whether that gap is closing or widening. What it means: This is the tracking indicator for the measure to restructure acceptance and load planning decisions around the U.S. departure stations. Only a narrowing gap between the two lines shows the measure is working. If both lines fall together, that is a factor common to the whole network, not an improvement on the U.S. routes.

10

前五大場站逐月異常率Monthly Mishandled Baggage Rate — Top Five Stations

用途：用統一縱軸把運量最大的五個場站畫在一起，看它們的相對位置如何隨月變化。 意義：這張圖取代了先前表格裡的迷你走勢線——迷你走勢線的縱軸是各站自己的範圍， 只能看方向、不能比高低；統一縱軸之後，「哪一站正在超車」一眼就看得出來， 這才是排優先順序時真正需要的資訊。 本圖固定以起程站歸戶（選站與畫線同口徑），與其餘趨勢圖一致，不隨上方「場站口徑」切換而變。Purpose: Plots the five largest stations by traffic on a single shared vertical axis, showing how their positions relative to one another shift from month to month. What it means: This chart replaces the sparklines used in the earlier table. A sparkline scales its axis to each station's own range, so it shows direction but not level. On a shared axis, which station is overtaking another is visible at a glance — and that is what is actually needed when setting priorities. This chart is always assigned on a departure station basis (station selection and plotting use the same basis), consistent with the other trend charts, and does not change with the station basis switch above.

11

Alaska／American 交接失敗逐月件數Alaska / American Interline Transfer Failures — Monthly Cases

用途：跨航交接失敗高度集中在兩家夥伴——Alaska 約占六成、American 約占三成。 這張圖把兩家分開逐月呈現。 意義：這是可以直接印出來帶去開會的佐證。「全期 419 件」是靜態指控， 「每個月幾件、有沒有在改善」才是談 SLA 與異常通報機制的籌碼。 若某家在特定月份暴增，也能對應到當時的班表或系統變更去查。Purpose: Interline transfer failures are heavily concentrated in two partners — Alaska at about 60% and American at about 30%. This chart shows each of them month by month. What it means: This is evidence that can be printed and taken straight into a meeting. "419 cases over the period" is a static accusation. How many each month, and whether it is improving, is what gives leverage in a conversation about SLAs and irregularity notification. If one partner spikes in a particular month, that can be matched against the schedule or system changes in force at the time.

09

作業條件趨勢Operating Condition Trends

機型／盤櫃／時段／機身 · 本期新接通Aircraft type / ULD / time band / airframe · newly connected this period

重點KEY POINT各時段破損率最高與最低相差 3.5 倍；本圖僅涵蓋可對接 P33 逐日班表的案件（全期約 83%），其餘不計入。The damage rate differs 3.5-fold between the best and worst time bands. This chart covers only cases that could be matched to the P33 daily flight schedule (about 83% of the period); the rest are excluded.

12

起飛時段別破損率逐月（每千件行李）Monthly Damage Rate by Departure Time Band (/1,000 Bags)

用途：把航班依起飛時刻分成深夜清晨、早班、午後、晚間四個時段，比較各時段的破損率。 這是本次接通 P33 逐日檔後才做得出來的新維度。 意義：時段差異若穩定存在，指向的是地勤班別、交接時點或尖峰壅塞， 而這三者都是可以直接查證與調整的作業條件——不像機型或航線那樣難以改變。 這是本次盤點中最具行動性的新線索。Purpose: Groups flights into four departure time bands — late night / early morning, morning, afternoon, evening — and compares the damage rate across them. This is a new dimension, made possible only by connecting the P33 daily file this period. What it means: A time band difference that persists points to ground handling shift patterns, handover timing or peak congestion. All three are operating conditions that can be verified and adjusted directly, unlike aircraft type or route. This is the most actionable new lead in this review.

13

機型別破損率逐月（每千件行李）Monthly Damage Rate by Aircraft Type (/1,000 Bags)

用途：比較各機型的行李破損率，分母為該機型當月的行李件數（P33 推估值）。 意義：機型差異可能反映貨艙結構、裝載方式或盤櫃配置。 但必須誠實標註限制：機型與航程長短高度重疊—— 窄體機幾乎全飛短程亞洲線、廣體機飛長程——因此差異可能反映的是航程長度而非機型本身， 不能據此宣稱某個機型比較會摔行李。要分離兩者需要同機型同時飛長短程的樣本，目前沒有。Purpose: Compares baggage damage rates by aircraft type. The denominator is that type's bags handled in the month (P33 estimate). What it means: Differences by type may reflect hold structure, loading method or ULD configuration. But the limitation has to be stated honestly: aircraft type and sector length overlap heavily — narrowbodies fly almost entirely short-haul Asian routes, widebodies fly long-haul — so the difference may reflect sector length rather than the aircraft type itself. It cannot be claimed on this basis that any given type damages more bags. Separating the two would require samples of the same type flying both long and short sectors, which do not currently exist.

14

ULD 盤櫃型別破損率逐月（每千件行李）Monthly Damage Rate by ULD Type (/1,000 Bags)

用途：比較不同行李盤櫃型別的破損率。 意義：這張圖與上一張其實是同一個變數。 實測顯示 AKH 只用於窄體機、AKE 只用於廣體機，兩者與機型完全共線， 所以「ULD 型別的差異」與「機型的差異」在數學上無法分離。 保留這張圖是為了讓盤櫃單位有自己的視角，但判讀時不可以把它當成獨立於機型的第二個發現。Purpose: Compares damage rates across baggage ULD types. What it means: This chart and the previous one are in fact the same variable. The data shows AKH is used only on narrowbodies and AKE only on widebodies, so ULD type is perfectly collinear with aircraft type. Differences by ULD type and differences by aircraft type therefore cannot be separated mathematically. The chart is kept so that the ULD function has its own view, but it must not be read as a second finding independent of aircraft type.

15

單機破損率排行（全期，非逐月）Damage Rate Ranking by Aircraft Registration (Full Period, Not Monthly)

用途：找出是否有特定機身異常——例如貨艙門、裝載裝置或內部結構有問題。 意義：這一張刻意不做逐月。 機隊規模與單機月航班數決定了每架每月的樣本量太小，逐月的率會被一兩件案件劇烈拉動， 畫成走勢線只會產生假訊號。正確作法是先用全期排行找出候選機身， 累積到十二個月以上再談逐月。本圖為觀察名單，不是結論。Purpose: Identifies whether any individual airframe stands out — for example a problem with a cargo door, loading equipment or internal structure. What it means: This chart is deliberately not shown monthly. Fleet size and monthly flights per aircraft make the per-aircraft monthly sample far too small; a monthly rate would swing violently on one or two cases, and a trend line would produce nothing but false signals. The correct approach is to use a full-period ranking to identify candidate airframes and revisit monthly views once twelve or more months have accumulated. This chart is a watch list, not a conclusion.

10

理賠與財務趨勢Claims and Financial Trends

賠付組合 · 處理量能 · 匯率效果Payout mix · processing capacity · exchange rate effect

重點KEY POINT末月受結案率影響（未結案者不計入），跨月比較請一併看第 11 區的成熟度圖。The final month is affected by the closure rate (open cases are excluded); read month-on-month comparisons alongside the maturity chart in Section 11.

16

每案平均賠償金額逐月Monthly Average Compensation per Case

用途：把「賠償總額」拆成「件數」與「每件多少錢」兩個因子中的後者。 分母只計有實際賠付的案件，避免被大量零賠付案件稀釋。 意義：總額下降有兩種完全不同的原因——案件變少（好事）或每件變便宜（可能是賠付標準改變）。 這張圖把兩者分開。若每案均額上升而件數下降，代表剩下的都是難處理的高額案，工作負荷未必變輕。Purpose: Total compensation breaks into two factors — how many cases, and how much each one costs. This chart is the second of those. The denominator counts only cases that actually resulted in a payout, so the figure is not diluted by the large number of zero-payout cases. What it means: A falling total has two entirely different possible causes — fewer cases (good news), or a lower cost per case (which may indicate a change in payout standards). This chart separates them. If the average per case rises while case counts fall, what remains are the difficult high-value cases, and the workload has not necessarily eased.

17

固定匯率 vs 實際匯率 賠償金額逐月Monthly Compensation at Constant vs Actual Exchange Rates

用途：賠償以多種外幣支付、再用各案建檔月的匯率換算台幣，因此金額走勢裡混入了匯率波動。 這張圖把全期改用同一組基準月匯率重算，與實際值並列。 意義：兩條線的差距就是純匯率效果。財報上稱為固定匯率（constant currency）， 用途是回答「賠付真的變多了，還是只是匯率變動」。若兩條線貼合，代表匯率不是干擾因素， 可以放心用實際值討論。Purpose: Compensation is paid in several currencies and converted to TWD at the rate for each case's creation month, so exchange rate movement is mixed into the trend. This chart recalculates the whole period using a single base month's rates and places the result alongside the actual figures. What it means: The gap between the two lines is the pure exchange rate effect. In financial reporting this is known as constant currency, and it answers the question of whether payouts genuinely rose or the exchange rate simply moved. If the two lines sit on top of each other, currency is not a confounding factor and the actual figures can be discussed with confidence.

18

賠償類別結構逐月占比Monthly Mix by Compensation Category

用途：看賠付組合的變化：現金、替換、遞送、維修、即時生活費、其他。 意義：組合比總額更能說明營運狀況。遞送費占比上升代表行李找回後要送到旅客手上的比例變高， 也就是延誤處理量增加；現金賠償占比上升代表找不回來或無法修復的比例變高，是更嚴重的訊號。 總額不變但組合往現金移動，實際上是惡化。Purpose: Tracks how the payout mix shifts across cash, replacement, delivery, repair, interim expenses and other. What it means: The mix says more about operations than the total does. A rising delivery share means a higher proportion of bags are being located and then delivered to the passenger — in other words, more delay handling. A rising cash share means a higher proportion cannot be found or cannot be repaired, which is the more serious signal. A flat total with the mix moving toward cash is in fact deterioration.

19

當月新增 vs 當月結案 vs 期末未結存量New Cases vs Cases Closed vs Open Case Backlog

用途：把理賠處理看成一個水池——新增是流入、結案是流出、未結存量是水位。 意義：存量開始累積時，代表處理量能跟不上新增速度， 而這個訊號會比平均結案天數更早出現——因為平均值只計算已結案的案件， 積壓中的案件根本不在分母裡。這是理賠人力配置的先行指標。 注意末月的結案數必然偏低（還沒結完），存量會相對偏高。Purpose: Treats claims handling as a tank — new cases flow in, closed cases flow out, and the open backlog is the water level. What it means: Once the backlog starts building, processing capacity is no longer keeping up with the rate of new cases. That signal appears earlier than average Days to Close, because the average counts only cases already closed — cases sitting in the backlog are not in the denominator at all. This is a leading indicator for claims staffing. Note that the final month's closed count is necessarily low (closing is still in progress), which makes its backlog look relatively high.

20

結案時效分布逐月（當日／1 日／2 日／3–7 日／8–21 日／逾 21 日）Monthly Distribution of Days to Close (Same Day / 1 / 2 / 3–7 / 8–21 / Over 21 Days)

用途：用堆疊圖看結案速度的分布，而不只是平均值。 意義：平均值會被極端值拉走——某站平均 45.8 天，可能是全部案件都慢， 也可能是少數幾件拖了半年。這兩種狀況的處理方式完全不同：前者要改流程，後者要個案盤點。 分布圖一眼就能分辨，而且「逾 21 日」那一塊的厚度變化，是客訴升級風險最直接的先行指標。Purpose: Uses a stacked chart to show the distribution of closing speed rather than just the average. What it means: Averages are pulled by extreme values. A station averaging 45.8 days may have every case running slow, or may have a handful of cases dragging on for half a year. The two situations call for completely different responses: the first needs a process change, the second a case-by-case review. A distribution tells them apart at a glance — and the changing thickness of the "over 21 days" band is the most direct leading indicator of escalation risk.

21

跨航分攤通知（Prorate Notice）狀態逐月Monthly Status of Interline Prorate Notices

用途：呈現 Interline Prorate Control List 的案件狀態與金額分布。 這份檔案本期首次納入分析。 意義：求償方向尚待確認。 這份「分攤通知」與跨航理賠追蹤區使用的 Delivery Control List 是兩份不同的表， 且欄位無法判斷是「我方向他航求償」還是「他航向我方求償」—— 兩者的解讀完全相反（逾期對前者是呆帳、對後者反而是免付）。 因此本圖只呈現狀態分布與金額，不做收付判讀，待運務處確認方向後再補上結論。Purpose: Shows the case status and amount distribution in the Interline Prorate Control List. This file is included in the analysis for the first time this period. What it means: The direction of the claim remains unconfirmed. This Prorate Notice list and the Delivery Control List used in the interline claims tracking section are two different files, and the available fields do not show whether these are claims we raise against other carriers or claims other carriers raise against us. The two readings are exact opposites — an expired item is unrecoverable in the first case, but simply not payable in the second. This chart therefore presents status distribution and amounts only, and draws no conclusion about receivable or payable. A conclusion will be added once Airport Operations Div. confirms the direction.

11

營運量能與資料品質趨勢Capacity and Data Quality Trends

分母端與資料可信度The denominator side and data credibility

重點KEY POINT期內旅客、行李、班次同步成長——率的改善有相當部分來自分母稀釋，不能全記在營運改善的帳上。Passengers, bags and flights all grew over the period — a material part of the improvement in the rate comes from denominator dilution and cannot all be credited to operations.

22

運量、行李件數、班次逐月（指數化，首月＝100）Monthly Passengers, Bags Handled and Flights (Indexed, First Month = 100)

用途：所有「率」的分母都在這張圖裡。三個數量級差很多（旅客數百萬、行李數百萬、班次數千）， 所以統一指數化成首月＝100 才能疊在一起比較成長速度。 意義：這是洞察一的關鍵佐證。主管一定會問「異常率下降，是分子變少還是分母變大」—— 若分母成長明顯快於案件下降，那率的改善有相當部分只是被稀釋出來的， 不能全部記在營運改善的帳上。Purpose: Every rate in this report has its denominator on this chart. The three series differ by orders of magnitude — passengers in the millions, bags in the millions, flights in the thousands — so all three are indexed to the first month = 100 to make their growth rates comparable on one axis. What it means: This is the key supporting evidence for Insight 1. Executives will ask whether the falling rate reflects a smaller numerator or a larger denominator. If denominator growth clearly outpaces the fall in cases, a substantial part of the rate improvement is simply dilution, and cannot all be credited to operational improvement.

23

每位旅客行李件數與每件重量逐月（指數化，首月＝100）Monthly Bags per Passenger and Weight per Bag (Indexed, First Month = 100)

用途：看旅客帶的行李是變多還是變重。來源為 P33 的系統推估值。 意義：行李變重會直接增加裝卸負荷與人員疲勞，是破損的先行指標。 建議與破損率走勢疊著看——如果重量先上升、破損率隨後跟上， 那麼旺季前的人力與設備準備就有明確的提前量可以規劃。Purpose: Shows whether passengers are carrying more bags or heavier ones. The source is the system estimate in P33. What it means: Heavier bags directly increase handling load and staff fatigue, making weight a leading indicator of damage. Read this alongside the damage rate trend. If weight rises first and the damage rate follows, there is a clear lead time within which staffing and equipment can be prepared ahead of the peak season.

24

超重行李收入逐月（現場 vs 預付 vs 活體動物）Monthly Excess Baggage Revenue (Onsite vs Prepaid vs AVIH)

用途：超重行李是實際的收入來源，也是非標準行李的處理負荷來源。 這張圖把三種收費方式分開看。 意義：兩個面向。收入面看季節性與旺季彈性；營運面看預付占比—— 預付比例上升代表更多旅客在出發前線上完成，可分流櫃檯尖峰、也讓收入提前確認。 現場收費比例高的站，是推廣線上預付最有價值的目標。Purpose: Excess Baggage (EB) is a real revenue stream and also a source of handling load for non-standard baggage. This chart separates the three ways it is collected. What it means: There are two angles. On revenue, it shows seasonality and peak-season elasticity. On operations, watch the prepaid share — a rising prepaid proportion means more passengers are completing payment online before departure, which relieves the counter peak and recognises the revenue earlier. Stations with a high onsite share are the most valuable targets for promoting online prepayment.

25

各月案件結案率（資料成熟度）Monthly Case Closure Rate (Data Maturity)

用途：把先前只寫在註記裡的「資料成熟度」獨立成圖。 意義：這張圖決定哪幾個月的金額可以相信。 結案率未達 95% 的月份，其賠償金額必然被低估，任何跨月的金額比較都會失真。 把它做成圖表而不是一段小字，是為了讓主管在看金額類圖表之前就先知道要打折扣， 而不是等到有人質疑才口頭解釋。Purpose: Promotes data maturity, previously buried in a footnote, into a chart of its own. What it means: This chart determines which months' amounts can be trusted. In any month whose closure rate is below 95%, compensation is necessarily understated, and any cross-month comparison of amounts will be distorted. Presenting this as a chart rather than a line of small print means executives know to discount those months before they look at any amount-based chart, instead of hearing a verbal explanation only once someone questions the figures.

26

起程站可解析率逐月（資料品質）Monthly Departure Station Resolution Rate (Data Quality)

用途：本報告的主指標「起程站異常率」依賴案件行程中的 JX 航班號能對應到航班表。 這張圖追蹤每個月能成功對應的比例。 意義：這是資料治理的監控指標。若某月解析率明顯下滑， 代表現場填寫航班號的品質變差，主指標的可信度會同步下降。 解析不到的案件不計入任何場站，因此不會灌水到某一站，但會讓分子整體偏低。Purpose: The report's primary metric — the mishandled baggage rate on a departure station basis — depends on matching the JX flight number in each case's itinerary to the flight schedule. This chart tracks the proportion successfully matched each month. What it means: This is a data governance monitoring metric. A clear fall in the resolution rate in any month means flight numbers are being recorded less reliably on the ground, and the credibility of the primary metric falls with it. Cases that cannot be resolved are assigned to no station at all, so they never inflate any single station, but they do leave the numerator low overall.

27

受影響行李件數 vs 案件數逐月Monthly Bags Affected vs Cases

用途：一件案件可能牽涉多件行李。全報告目前都以「案件數」計算， 這張圖並列真正受影響的行李件數。 意義：兩條線的距離就是「每案平均行李件數」。 對旅客服務而言案件數是對的單位（一個旅客一個案）， 但對作業負荷與賠付風險而言行李件數才是對的單位。 若兩線開始分岔，代表多件行李的案件變多，單件處理成本會上升。Purpose: A single case can involve more than one bag. The report counts cases throughout; this chart places the number of bags actually affected alongside them. What it means: The gap between the two lines is the average number of bags per case. For passenger service, cases are the right unit — one passenger, one case. For handling load and payout exposure, bags are the right unit. If the two lines begin to diverge, multi-bag cases are becoming more common and the cost of handling each case will rise.

七大核心洞察Seven Core Insights

依當期 1–7 月數字撰寫Written from this period's Jan–Jul figures

重點KEY POINT異常率下降已排除「航網組合」與「結案延遲」兩種假象，但本期無對應改善專案，仍不可當成營運績效。The fall in the mishandled baggage rate has been cleared of both the network-mix and the closing-lag artefacts, but with no corresponding improvement project this period it still cannot be presented as operational performance.

1

異常率七個月持續下降，且已排除「航網組合」與「結案延遲」兩種假象——但目前還不能當成營運績效

JX 可控起程站異常率由 1 月 2.63／千客降至 7 月 1.87（−28.9%），破損率同步由 1.99‰ 降至 1.61‰。我們做了三重檢定確認這不是統計錯覺：① 月份以「建檔月」歸戶，案件一經建檔即不再變動，因此與結案進度無關（會受結案影響的只有金額）；② 把各站的率固定用 1 月的運量權重重新加權後，仍由 2.63 降至 1.90（−27.6%），與實際的 −28.9% 幾乎相同，代表下降不是「高風險航線占比變小」造成的組合效果；③ 31 個離站量達標的場站中有 24 站末月低於首月，各站率中位數由 3.38 降至 2.38，是普遍性而非個別站拉動。七個月的值也全數落在 ±2 標準差的管制界線內（平均 2.20，界線 1.69–2.71），屬穩定趨勢移動而非突發事件。

但下降的原因目前無法確認。運務處已確認本期並無針對行李的改善專案，因此不宜將此下降列為成效。以下三種解釋同樣與資料相符、且都尚未被排除：(i) 破損現場判定尺度或建單標準改變——破損案占全部 76.6%，是全場站率的主要驅動，若各站對「什麼程度算破損」的認定收緊，率就會下降而實際品質未變；(ii) 分母成長稀釋——期內離站旅客由 468,902 成長至 563,235（+20%），而案件僅由 1,388 降至 1,138（−18%），率的下降有相當部分來自分母擴張；(iii) 七個月無法分離季節性，也無法排除新機隊與新航線比重上升的影響。

待查證（建議列為下一期必辦）：① 取得 2025 年 1–7 月同一套指標做同期比較，若年年皆有此型態即為季節性；② 向各站確認破損建單標準與照片留存規則本期是否調整；③ 檢視新機（含新交機）與新航線在期內的運量占比變化。
現象確認 · 成因待查證
2

真正的風險集中點是美國線起程站，而不是報案量最大的站

SEA 10.17、LAX 9.40、SFO 6.48、PHX 5.68、ONT 4.25／千離站客——美國五站僅占全場站運量 6.0%（213,647 客），卻占 JX 可控案件 21.2%（1,650 件），合計率 7.72‰＝全場站 2.19 的 3.5 倍。若改用報案站口徑，SEA 只有 2.03、看起來毫無問題，因為西雅圖出發的行李問題是在台北或旅客最終目的地才被發現的。這正是本報告以起程站為主指標的原因。

對應的航線也一致：SEA-TPE 每千離站客 18.36 件、LAX-TPE 10.06、PHX-TPE 與 SFO-TPE 各 8.15，全部集中在美西往台北的長程回程段。

起程站歸戶 · 美西集中
3

「艙位／重量限制」的追責鏈已經完整——出事在美西、報案在克拉克，主責不在台北

RL 65（Space/Weight restrictions）期內 358 件。改用起程站歸戶後，成因鏈第一次看得清楚：起程站為 LAX 163、SFO 98、SGN 50、TPE 41；報案站為 CRK 240、TPE 40、CGK 30；首段航班為 JX1（LAX-TPE）161、JX11（SFO-TPE）94。也就是說：行李在洛杉磯或舊金山因長程航班的配載／載重限制未能上機，旅客搭同一班抵台轉機後，在最終目的地（多為克拉克）才發現行李沒到。

這修正了上一期的判斷。上一期只能看報案站與首段航班，把主責指向台北站與 JX789（TPE-CRK）的裝載；改以起程站歸戶後可以確認，行李根本沒有離開美西。改善與追責應落在美西三站的配載決策——特別是旅客行李相對於貨物的拉下順序——而非台北站或克拉克站。需調閱 JX1／JX11 的 Load Sheet 才能確認實際拉下的品項與順序（WorldTracer 不記錄拉下站）。

追責鏈修正 · 主責在美西
4

破損主導是本網最大的結構特徵，且集中在少數長程航段

破損 6,595 件占全部 76.9%（依 RL 分類為 76.6%），全球基準僅 18%；延誤僅 23.1%（全球 74%）。全場站破損率 1.74‰。以航段歸戶：SEA-TPE 4.83‰、TPE-HKG 3.91、KUL-TPE 3.67、BKK-TPE 3.42、HKG-TPE 3.24。破損不歸單站是因為它可能發生於出發站裝載、運送途中或抵達站卸載三個環節，需實地查核（如監看裝卸錄影）才能釐清。

延誤側的成因結構也透露資料特性：轉接類占延誤案 41.7%，與全球 41% 幾乎相同；但「營運／設備／天候」30.5% 遠高於全球 10%，而「未能裝載」僅 1.5% 遠低於全球 17%。這兩者很可能存在代碼填寫習慣的重疊（本網把裝不上去記成「艙位／重量限制」而非「未能裝載」），判讀時宜合併看待，不宜單獨宣稱某一項優於或劣於業界。

破損主導 · 代碼填寫習慣
5

跨航交接失敗全數集中在美西與兩家夥伴；催收有實質進展，但仍有呆帳

「未從他航收到行李」（RL 54）與「他航作業錯誤」（RL 77）合計 676 件（占全部案件 7.9%），已自所有站別率剔除以免誤責。依交接站：SEA 427 件（63%）、SFO 87、PHX 60、LAX 36；依夥伴：AS（Alaska Airlines）419 件（63%）、AA（American Airlines）180 件（27%），兩家合計九成。

跨航理賠分攤 598 件：已結案 271 件（US$6,853）、資料收集中 246 件（US$6,862）、已逾期 36 件（US$876）、遭他航以資料不足拒賠 45 件。與上一期（1–6 月）相比，「資料收集中」由 307 件降至 198 件、「結案」由 186 件增至 271 件，催收確有實質進展；但逾期件數由 29 件增至 36 件、全部集中在 1–3 月建檔的案件，代表當時的補件沒有在索賠期限內完成，該部分金額恐已無法收回。

他航責任 · 催收有進展
6

北美結案時效是理賠流程問題，與行李找不找得到無關

平均結案天數：PHX 45.8 天（56 件）、SFO 19.0（187 件）、LAX 16.0（178 件）、ONT 13.3（88 件）、SEA 10.6（97 件），對比 TPE 4.7、CRK 2.3、全場站平均 5.2 天。結案天數計算的是「建檔日到結案日」，反映的是賠付授權與文件往返效率，並非行李尋回速度——PHX 的 45.8 天為全場站最長、接近全場站平均的九倍。此層以報案站歸戶，因處理與賠付責任在受理站。

需注意 7 月案件結案率僅 88.8%（1–6 月為 97.2–99.8%），尚未結案者不計入平均，因此近月的平均結案天數會偏低（結得慢的還沒進來），跨月比較時須留意。

理賠流程 · 非尋回速度
7

超重行李是一門「由外站承接」的生意；自助行李託運則在母基地明顯落後

超重行李收入 98,912,799 元、18,606 筆、每筆 5,316 元、每位旅客 27.8 元；現場收費 49.3%、預付 47.1%、活體動物運送 3.6%。收入高度集中於 TPE（44,646,200 元、45.1%），但 TPE 每千客超重僅 2.8 件、遠低於全場站 5.23——因為超重費在旅客行程起點站的報到櫃檯收取，台北出發多為本地外出旅客、行李較輕；旅客回程在國外採購的超重則記在外站（SGN 每千客 34.3、PHX 22.2、LAX 21.0）。若改以「TPE 為到達站」統計，同一批行李的超重達 12,120 筆＝出發的 2.8 倍，可見台北龐大客量的超重處理負荷其實落在回程外站。

自助行李託運（SBD）全場站採用率 13.2%，七個月由 11.3% 升至 14.0%。但這個數字主要反映設備覆蓋、不是旅客意願：託運量達標的 34 個場站中，期內有自助託運紀錄的只有 7 站（NGO 77.3%、KIX 63.0%、FUK 53.3%、DAD 22.1%、TPE 19.1%、BKK 15.5%、HKG 8.3%），其餘 27 站為 0 件——包含東京成田（NRT）與全部五個美國站，合計 1,688,756 件行李、占全場站託運量 44.5%（有設備的 7 站則占 55.5%）。這些站應解讀為「該機場未配置或未啟用自助託運設備」，而非旅客不願使用。

因此「日本站採用率高」並不成立——同屬日本的成田為 0，設備配置是逐站而非逐國的。真正可行動的是母基地 TPE：設備已在、採用率僅 19.1%，卻承擔全場站最大託運量（1,639,674 件），採用率每提升 1 個百分點約可減少 16,397 件人工櫃檯處理量。這屬於「設備已在、使用率待提升」的問題，改善成本遠低於在無設備站新設。

超重外站承接 · 自助託運落後
1

The mishandled baggage rate has fallen for seven consecutive months, and both the network-mix and the closure-lag artefacts have been ruled out — but it cannot yet be counted as operational performance

The JX-controllable mishandled baggage rate on a Departure Station basis fell from 2.63 per 1,000 pax in Jan to 1.87 in Jul (−28.9%), and the damage rate fell in step from 1.99 to 1.61 per 1,000 bags. Three tests were run to confirm that this is not a statistical illusion. ① Cases are assigned to their creation month, and a case's month never changes once it is created, so the series is independent of closure progress (only the amounts are affected by closure). ② Re-weighting every station's rate with January's traffic weights still gives a fall from 2.63 to 1.90 (−27.6%), almost identical to the actual −28.9%, which means the decline is not a mix effect produced by high-risk routes shrinking as a share of the network. ③ Of the 31 stations meeting the departing-passenger threshold, 24 ended the period below their first month, and the median station rate fell from 3.38 to 2.38 — the decline is broad-based rather than driven by a few stations. All seven monthly values also sit inside the ±2 standard deviation control limits (mean 2.20, limits 1.69–2.71), which is consistent with a stable trend movement and not with a one-off event.

The reason for the decline cannot be established at this point. Airport Operations Div. has confirmed that no baggage improvement project ran during the period, so the decline should not be recorded as a result. The three explanations below are equally consistent with the data, and none of them has been ruled out. (i) A change in how damage is judged on the spot or in how damage reports are raised — damage cases make up 76.6% of all cases and are the main driver of the network rate, so if stations tightened their view of what counts as damage, the rate would fall while actual quality was unchanged. (ii) Denominator dilution — departing passengers grew from 468,902 to 563,235 (+20%) over the period while cases fell only from 1,388 to 1,138 (−18%), so a substantial part of the fall in the rate comes from the expanding denominator. (iii) Seven months are not enough to separate seasonality, and the rising share of new aircraft and new routes cannot be excluded either.

To be verified (recommended as mandatory for the next edition): ① obtain the same set of metrics for Jan–Jul 2025 for a like-for-like comparison — if the pattern recurs year after year it is seasonality; ② confirm with each station whether damage reporting standards and photo retention rules were changed during the period; ③ review how the traffic share of new aircraft (including newly delivered airframes) and new routes moved over the period.
Observation confirmed · cause to be verified
2

The real concentration of risk sits at the U.S. departure stations, not at the stations where the most reports are filed

SEA 10.17, LAX 9.40, SFO 6.48, PHX 5.68, ONT 4.25 per 1,000 departing passengers — the five U.S. stations carry only 6.0% of network traffic (213,647 passengers) but account for 21.2% of JX-controllable cases (1,650 cases), a combined rate of 7.72 per 1,000 = 3.5 times the network figure of 2.19. On a Reporting Station basis SEA shows only 2.03 and looks entirely unproblematic, because baggage problems originating in Seattle are discovered in Taipei or at the passenger's final destination. This is precisely why this report uses Departure Station as its primary basis.

The route view agrees: SEA-TPE 18.36 per 1,000 departing passengers, LAX-TPE 10.06, and PHX-TPE and SFO-TPE 8.15 each — all concentrated on the long-haul return legs from the U.S. West Coast to Taipei.

Departure Station basis · U.S. West Coast concentration
3

The accountability chain for space/weight restrictions is now complete — the event happens on the U.S. West Coast and the report is filed at Clark, and the primary responsibility does not sit with Taipei

RL 65 (Space/Weight restrictions) accounts for 358 cases in the period. On a Departure Station basis the causal chain is visible for the first time. By Departure Station: LAX 163, SFO 98, SGN 50, TPE 41. By Reporting Station: CRK 240, TPE 40, CGK 30. By first flight of the itinerary: JX1 (LAX-TPE) 161, JX11 (SFO-TPE) 94. In other words, the bag fails to board at Los Angeles or San Francisco because of load-planning or weight restrictions on the long-haul flight; the passenger travels on that same flight, connects in Taipei, and only discovers at the final destination — usually Clark — that the bag has not arrived.

This corrects the conclusion of the previous edition. With only Reporting Station and first flight available, the previous edition pointed the primary responsibility at Taipei station and at loading on JX789 (TPE-CRK); on a Departure Station basis it is now confirmed that the bags never left the U.S. West Coast. Improvement and accountability belong with the load-planning decisions at the three U.S. West Coast stations — in particular the order in which passenger baggage is offloaded relative to cargo — and not with Taipei or Clark. The load sheets for JX1 and JX11 have to be retrieved before the items actually offloaded and the order of offload can be confirmed (WorldTracer does not record the offload station).

Accountability chain corrected · responsibility on the U.S. West Coast
4

Damage dominance is the biggest structural feature of this network, and it is concentrated on a small number of long-haul segments

Damage accounts for 6,595 cases, 76.9% of the total (76.6% when classified by RL code), against a global benchmark of only 18%; delayed/missing is just 23.1% (global 74%). The network damage rate is 1.74 per 1,000 bags. On a Segment basis: SEA-TPE 4.83, TPE-HKG 3.91, KUL-TPE 3.67, BKK-TPE 3.42, HKG-TPE 3.24 per 1,000 bags. Damage cannot be assigned to a single station because it may occur during loading at the departure station, in transit, or during unloading at the arrival station; on-site verification (such as reviewing loading and unloading video) is needed to establish which.

The cause structure on the delay side also reveals a characteristic of the data: transfer mishandling accounts for 41.7% of delay cases, almost identical to the global 41%; but Airport / Customs / Weather / Space-weight restriction at 30.5% is far above the global 10%, while failure to load at 1.5% is far below the global 17%. The two very probably overlap through coding habit — this network records a bag that could not be loaded as a space/weight restriction rather than as a failure to load — so they should be read together, and neither should be claimed on its own to be better or worse than the industry.

Damage-dominated · coding habit
5

Interline transfer failures sit entirely on the U.S. West Coast and with two partners; recovery follow-up has made real progress, but unrecoverable amounts remain

Bag not received from another carrier (RL 54) and other-carrier handling error (RL 77) together account for 676 cases (7.9% of all cases) and have been removed from every station rate so that liability is not misassigned. By transfer station: SEA 427 cases (63%), SFO 87, PHX 60, LAX 36. By partner: AS (Alaska Airlines) 419 cases (63%) and AA (American Airlines) 180 cases (27%), the two together nine tenths of the total.

Interline baggage claim proration covers 598 cases: 271 closed (US$6,853), 246 collecting documentation (US$6,862), 36 expired (US$876), and 45 rejected by the other carrier for insufficient documentation. Against the previous edition (Jan–Jun), collecting documentation fell from 307 to 198 cases and closed rose from 186 to 271, so recovery follow-up has made real progress. Expired cases, however, rose from 29 to 36 and are all cases created in Jan–Mar, which means the supporting documents were not completed within the claim deadline and those amounts are likely to be unrecoverable.

Other-carrier liability · recovery progressing
6

North American closure timeliness is a claims process problem and has nothing to do with whether the bag is found

Average Days to Close: PHX 45.8 days (56 cases), SFO 19.0 (187 cases), LAX 16.0 (178 cases), ONT 13.3 (88 cases), SEA 10.6 (97 cases), against TPE 4.7, CRK 2.3 and a network average of 5.2 days. Days to Close measures the interval from creation date to closure date; it reflects payout authorisation and document turnaround, not the speed at which bags are recovered — PHX at 45.8 days is the longest in the network and close to nine times the network average. This layer is assigned on a Reporting Station basis, because handling and payout responsibility sit with the station that takes the report.

Note that the July closure rate is only 88.8% (97.2–99.8% for Jan–Jun). Cases not yet closed are excluded from the average, so the average Days to Close for recent months is understated (the slow ones have not entered yet), and this has to be kept in mind when comparing across months.

Claims process · not recovery speed
7

Excess baggage is a business carried by the outstations; Self Bag Drop, by contrast, lags clearly at the home base

Excess Baggage revenue is TWD 98,912,799 from 18,606 transactions, TWD 5,316 per transaction and TWD 27.8 per passenger; 49.3% onsite, 47.1% prepaid, 3.6% Animal in Hold. Revenue is heavily concentrated at TPE (TWD 44,646,200, 45.1%), yet TPE records only 2.8 excess baggage transactions per 1,000 passengers, far below the network figure of 5.23 — the fee is collected at the check-in counter of the first station of the passenger's itinerary, and passengers departing Taipei are mostly outbound locals travelling light. Excess weight from shopping abroad is booked at the outstations on the return leg (SGN 34.3 per 1,000 passengers, PHX 22.2, LAX 21.0). Counting the same bags with TPE as the arrival station gives 12,120 transactions, 2.8 times the departure figure, which shows that the excess baggage workload generated by Taipei's large traffic base actually falls on the outstations on the return leg.

Self Bag Drop (SBD) adoption network-wide is 13.2%, rising from 11.3% to 14.0% over the seven months. But this figure mainly reflects equipment coverage, not passenger willingness: of the 34 stations meeting the checked-baggage threshold, only 7 recorded any self bag drop during the period (NGO 77.3%, KIX 63.0%, FUK 53.3%, DAD 22.1%, TPE 19.1%, BKK 15.5%, HKG 8.3%), while the remaining 27 stations recorded zero — including Tokyo Narita (NRT) and all five U.S. stations, together 1,688,756 bags, or 44.5% of network checked baggage (the 7 equipped stations account for the other 55.5%). These stations should be read as airports where self bag drop equipment is not installed or not activated, not as passengers declining to use it.

The claim that adoption is high at Japanese stations therefore does not hold — Narita, also in Japan, is at zero, and equipment is deployed station by station, not country by country. What is genuinely actionable is the home base (TPE): the equipment is already in place, adoption is only 19.1%, and the station handles the largest checked baggage volume in the network (1,639,674 bags). Each percentage point of adoption removes roughly 16,397 bags from agent-assisted counter handling. This is an equipment-already-in-place, utilisation-to-be-raised problem, and it costs far less to address than installing equipment at stations that have none.

Excess baggage carried by outstations · Self Bag Drop lagging
25

改善效益情境試算Improvement Scenario Modelling

情境假設 · 固定全期全場站Scenario assumptions · full period, network-wide

重點KEY POINT本區以全期全場站資料計算、不隨篩選器變動；只呈現件數與金額，不換算人力工時或成本節省（無工時基準）。This section is calculated on the full period and the whole network and does not change with the filters. It presents case counts and amounts only, with no conversion to man-hours or cost savings — there is no labour baseline.

美西五站
起程異常率改善Five U.S. stations
departure-station rate improvement 0%
全場站
破損案件改善Network-wide
damage case reduction 0%
跨航未收回款
回收率Outstanding interline
receivables recovery rate 0%

試算母體＝JX 可控案件（已剔除他航交接失敗 RL 54／77、且起程站可解析），與第 01 區主指標同口徑。「預估節省賠償」係逐案以該案實際賠償金加權後加總，不是用平均值乘件數。兩個件數槓桿的作用對象重疊（美西五站的破損案同時被兩者涵蓋），故採「至少被一項措施攔下」的機率 1−(1−p₁)(1−p₂) 計算期望值，不會重複計數。本區僅呈現件數與金額，不換算人力工時或成本節省——現有資料沒有任何工時基準或費率，換算出來的數字無法查證。滑桿為情境假設而非預測，改善幅度能否達成須由各執行單位評估。The modelling population is JX-controllable cases (interline transfer failures RL 54 / 77 excluded, and the departure station resolvable), on the same basis as the primary metric in Section 01. "Estimated compensation saved" is summed case by case, weighted by each case's actual compensation, not an average multiplied by a case count. The two case-count levers overlap (damage cases at the five U.S. stations are covered by both), so the expected value is calculated from the probability of being caught by at least one measure, 1−(1−p₁)(1−p₂), and nothing is double counted. This section shows case counts and amounts only and does not convert them into labour hours or cost savings—the available data contains no labour-hour baseline and no rates, so any converted figure would be unverifiable. The sliders are scenario assumptions, not forecasts; whether the improvement levels are achievable must be assessed by the units that would carry them out.

26

行動建議Recommended Actions

依投報率排序Ranked by return on effort

重點KEY POINT建議依投報比排序，並標明權責單位與觀察指標；本區不進主管版。The recommendations are ranked by return on effort and name the owning unit and the metric to watch; this section is not included in the management edition.

最高投報

1. 以「美國線起程站」為單位重整收運與配載決策

美國五站僅占運量 6.0% 卻占 JX 可控案件 21.2%、率為全場站 3.5 倍，是全場站唯一可以用「一個決策改變一整群案件」的著力點。具體做法：逐班檢視 JX1（LAX-TPE）與 JX11（SFO-TPE）的 Load Sheet 與實際拉下品項，釐清旅客行李相對於貨物的拉下順序；由外站運務單位與配載／載重平衡單位共同訂定「旅客行李優先於貨物」的例外條件與核決層級，並要求拉下時回填拉下站（現行 WorldTracer 不記錄，事後無法追溯）。西雅圖另需與 Alaska Airlines 就交接時限與異常通報方式建立書面約定（見第 4 項）。

美國五站起程站異常率由 7.72‰ 降至 4.0‰ 以下；RL 65「艙位／重量限制」由 358 件降至 200 件以下。
最高投報

2. 回溯 3 月 LAX 單月暴衝事件

LAX 3 月起程站異常率飆至 16.91‰（其他月份為 5.10–11.08），成因高度集中：該月「設備故障」（RL 64）42 件、其中 JX1 單一航班占 33 件；同月「艙位／重量限制」（RL 65）另有 55 件。這是本期最明確的單一事件訊號，且屬於可以查清楚的類型。做法：調閱 3 月 JX1 的裝載紀錄與洛杉磯站的行李系統／設備維修紀錄，確認是否為單一設備故障期，並檢視當時的替代作業程序。

兩週內完成事件報告，明確結論為「單一設備故障」或「常態性作業問題」，後者須另立改善案。
高投報

3. 縮短北美理賠授權鏈

PHX 平均結案 45.8 天、SFO 19.0 天、LAX 16.0 天，而全場站平均僅 5.2 天。結案慢不影響行李是否找回，但直接影響旅客感受與客訴升級風險，且改善成本低——問題在授權門檻與文件往返，不需要新增設備或人力。做法：由行李服務單位盤點北美五站的賠付核決層級與所需文件，將小額賠付（例如 5,000 元以下）下放至站級核決，並對超過 T+7 未結案者建立每週清單追蹤。PHX 樣本僅 56 件卻平均 45.8 天，宜先個案盤點是否為少數極端案件拉高平均。

北美五站平均結案天數由 18.4 天（606 件加權平均）降至 7 天以下；無單一案件結案超過 30 天。
高投報

4. 建立跨航催收的補件 SLA 與逾期預警

目前「資料收集中」246 件、US$6,862 帳齡持續增長，且已有 36 件、US$876 逾期恐成呆帳。案件高度集中於 AS（370 件）與 AA（163 件）兩家，屬於「少數對象、可制度化」的問題。做法：對 AS／AA 建立月度對帳會議與單一聯絡窗口；內部訂定補件 T+14 的 SLA，並在索賠期限前 30 天自動產生預警清單（現行 Interline Delivery Control List 已有 DEADLINE 欄位，可直接據以排程）。已逾期的 36 件應個案確認是否仍有申訴空間，無法收回者列為損失並回溯流程缺口。

逾期件數歸零；未收回金額（收集中＋逾期）由 US$7,738 降低 50% 以上。
中投報

5. 推廣台北站自助行李託運

TPE 自助託運採用率僅 19.1%，卻承擔全場站最大的託運量（1,639,674 件）。以規模計算，採用率每提升 1 個百分點約減少 16,397 件人工櫃檯處理量；若由 19.1% 提升至 30%，約可減少 17.9 萬件的櫃檯作業負荷。之所以把 TPE 列為第一優先，是因為它屬於「設備已在、使用率待提升」——做法：盤點第一／第二航廈自助託運機台數量與尖峰使用率（目前 T1 206,154 件、T2 91,324 件、A1 僅 12,527 件），確認瓶頸是機台數量、動線指引或旅客不熟悉。至於期內自助託運為 0 件的 27 個站（含東京成田與全部美國站），需要的是設備投資決策而非推廣，成本量級完全不同，建議另案評估、優先順序依託運量與現行櫃檯人力成本排序。並與第 23 區的報到通路交叉檢視——報到數位化與行李託運自助化是兩件不同的事，本網明顯落後於後者。

TPE 自助行李託運採用率由 19.1% 提升至 30%；全場站由 13.2% 提升至 20%。
中投報

6. 稽核各站破損建單標準的一致性

這一項是為了確認洞察一的下降是真的。破損案占全部案件 76.6%，是全場站異常率的主要驅動；若各站對「什麼程度算破損」的判定尺度在期內收緊，率會下降而實際品質未變，等於用錯誤的訊號指導決策。做法：由行李服務單位抽樣複核各站的 DPR 建單標準、照片留存規則與現場判定流程，確認 1–7 月間是否有任何調整（含人員輪替造成的實質差異），並書面化統一標準作為後續期間的比較基準。

完成各站標準一致性確認並書面化；下一期報告可明確排除或確認「判定尺度改變」這個解釋。
低成本必辦

7. 向資訊／地服系統釋疑報到通路代碼定義

Check-in 報表提供六個通路代碼（JFE／WEB／MOB／Kiosk／ACI／EDS），但來源檔沒有中文定義，且資料中沒有獨立的「人工櫃檯」欄位——六者合計已涵蓋 98.8% 的報到旅客。這使得「自助報到比例」這個數字完全取決於代碼定義：若 JFE（占 44.4%）實際上是櫃檯人員操作的前台系統，自助比例會大幅下降。另有兩個異常需釋疑：MOB 行動報到全期為 0（App 報到可能被歸入 WEB 或 JFE，導致行動報到被低估）；ACI 自 6 月才出現（0% → 6 月 7.3% → 7 月 13.2%），同期 JFE 與 WEB 同步下滑，型態上像是新通路上線或欄位歸類調整，須確認是真實的旅客行為移轉還是統計歸屬變更。

取得六個通路的正式中文定義與自助／臨櫃歸屬，並據以更新第 23 區分類（程式已將分類集中於單一設定點，取得定義後可一行修正）。
Highest ROI

1. Rebuild acceptance and load-planning decisions around the U.S. departure stations

The five U.S. stations carry only 6.0% of traffic but account for 21.2% of JX-controllable cases, at 3.5 times the network rate; they are the one place in the network where a single decision can move an entire group of cases. Specifically: review flight by flight the load sheets and the items actually offloaded for JX1 (LAX-TPE) and JX11 (SFO-TPE) to establish the order in which passenger baggage is offloaded relative to cargo; have the outstation airport operations teams and the load control / weight and balance teams jointly define the exception conditions and approval level under which passenger baggage takes priority over cargo; and require the offload station to be entered whenever a bag is offloaded (WorldTracer does not record it today, so it cannot be traced afterwards). Seattle additionally needs a written agreement with Alaska Airlines on transfer time limits and on how irregularities are notified (see item 4).

Mishandled baggage rate at the five U.S. departure stations down from 7.72 to below 4.0 per 1,000; RL 65 space/weight restrictions down from 358 cases to below 200.
Highest ROI

2. Investigate the single-month spike at LAX in March

The LAX departure station rate spiked to 16.91 per 1,000 in March (5.10–11.08 in the other months), with a highly concentrated cause: 42 equipment failure cases (RL 64) that month, of which 33 were on the single flight JX1, plus a further 55 space/weight restriction cases (RL 65) in the same month. This is the clearest single-event signal in the period, and it is of a type that can be established conclusively. Method: retrieve the March loading records for JX1 together with the baggage system and equipment maintenance records at Los Angeles, confirm whether there was a single equipment failure window, and review the contingency procedures in force at the time.

Event report completed within two weeks, with an explicit conclusion of either a single equipment failure or a recurring operational problem; the latter requires a separate improvement case.
High ROI

3. Shorten the North American claims authorisation chain

PHX averages 45.8 days to close, SFO 19.0 days and LAX 16.0 days, against a network average of only 5.2 days. Slow closure does not affect whether a bag is recovered, but it directly affects passenger perception and the risk of complaint escalation, and it is cheap to fix — the problem lies in authorisation thresholds and document turnaround, not in new equipment or headcount. Method: have the baggage services team map the payout approval levels and required documents at the five North American stations, delegate small payouts (for example below TWD 5,000) to station-level approval, and set up a weekly tracking list for any case still open at T+7. PHX shows 45.8 days on a sample of only 56 cases, so an individual case review should first establish whether a few extreme cases are pulling the average up.

Average Days to Close at the five North American stations down from 18.4 days (weighted average over 606 cases) to below 7 days; no single case open longer than 30 days.
High ROI

4. Establish a documentation SLA and an expiry alert for interline recovery

There are currently 246 cases collecting documentation, worth US$6,862, whose ageing keeps growing, and 36 cases worth US$876 have already expired and may become unrecoverable. Cases are heavily concentrated on AS (370 cases) and AA (163 cases), which makes this a few-counterparties, can-be-systematised problem. Method: set up a monthly reconciliation meeting and a single point of contact with AS and AA; define an internal T+14 documentation SLA; and generate an alert list automatically 30 days before the claim deadline (the Interline Delivery Control List already carries a DEADLINE field that can be scheduled from directly). The 36 expired cases should be reviewed individually to see whether any appeal is still possible, with anything unrecoverable written off and the process gap traced back.

Expired cases reduced to zero; amounts not yet recovered (collecting plus expired) down by more than 50% from US$7,738.
Moderate ROI

5. Promote Self Bag Drop at Taipei

TPE self bag drop adoption is only 19.1%, yet the station handles the largest checked baggage volume in the network (1,639,674 bags). At that scale each percentage point of adoption removes roughly 16,397 bags from agent-assisted counter handling; moving from 19.1% to 30% would take about 179,000 bags off the counters. TPE is the first priority because it is an equipment-already-in-place, utilisation-to-be-raised case. Method: count the self bag drop units and their peak utilisation in Terminal 1 and Terminal 2 (currently T1 206,154 bags, T2 91,324 bags, A1 only 12,527 bags) and establish whether the bottleneck is the number of units, wayfinding, or passenger unfamiliarity. For the 27 stations with zero self bag drop in the period (including Tokyo Narita and all five U.S. stations), what is needed is an equipment investment decision rather than promotion; the cost is of an entirely different order, so it should be assessed separately and prioritised by checked baggage volume and current counter staffing cost. This should also be read across with the check-in channel view in Section 23 — digital check-in and self bag drop are two different things, and this network is clearly behind on the latter.

TPE Self Bag Drop adoption up from 19.1% to 30%; network-wide up from 13.2% to 20%.
Moderate ROI

6. Audit the consistency of damage reporting standards across stations

This item exists to confirm whether the decline in insight 1 is real. Damage accounts for 76.6% of all cases and is the main driver of the network mishandled baggage rate; if stations tightened their judgement of what counts as damage during the period, the rate would fall while actual quality was unchanged, which would mean decisions guided by a false signal. Method: have the baggage services team sample and re-review each station's DPR reporting standards, photo retention rules and on-the-spot judgement process, confirm whether anything was changed between January and July (including material differences caused by staff rotation), and set out a single written standard as the comparison baseline for future periods.

Consistency of station standards confirmed and documented; the next edition can explicitly rule out or confirm the changed-judgement-threshold explanation.
Low-cost, must do

7. Obtain definitions of the check-in channel codes from IT and the ground handling systems

The Check-in report provides six channel codes (JFE / WEB / MOB / Kiosk / ACI / EDS), but the source file carries no definitions, and the data contains no separate agent-assisted counter field — the six together already cover 98.8% of checked-in passengers. This makes the self-service check-in share entirely dependent on how the codes are defined: if JFE (44.4%) is in fact a front-office system operated by counter staff, the self-service share would fall sharply. Two anomalies also need clarification: MOB mobile check-in is zero for the whole period (app check-in may be recorded under WEB or JFE, understating mobile check-in), and ACI appears only from June (0% → 7.3% in Jun → 13.2% in Jul) while JFE and WEB decline in step, a pattern that looks like a new channel going live or a change in field classification; it must be confirmed whether this is a genuine shift in passenger behaviour or a change in statistical attribution.

Obtain the official definitions of the six channels and their self-service / agent-assisted attribution, and update the classification in Section 23 accordingly (the code already concentrates the classification in a single configuration point, so it can be corrected in one line once the definitions are available).
27

✓ Data period 2026-01-01 to 2026-07-31 (seven complete months); all 28 month-by-month reconciliation checks agree

  • Month-by-month reconciliation (the most important check this period): every month of all seven monthly source files was reconciled against that file's own total row before being used — departing passengers, bags handled, excess baggage amount and excess baggage transactions from P31Segment (7 months × 4 items), the cabin class rows of Check-in against its total row (7 items), the SBD totals in Baggage (7 items), and the detail against the total in P31OnD (7 items), 28 checks in all, every one of them agreeing. Denominators for the full period: departing passengers 3,556,420, bags handled 3,800,680.
  • Cross-validation against the previous edition: the Jan–Jun totals of the new monthly files were compared with the previously validated figures — departing passengers 2,993,185 and bags 3,226,526 match exactly, which confirms that the monthly split is faithful. Excess baggage amount is TWD 85,548,822 against TWD 85,568,551 (TWD 19,729 lower, 0.023%) and transactions are 16,073 against 16,076 (3 fewer); the differences come from late entries or corrections in the source system between the two extracts, are too small to affect any conclusion, and the new values are used this period.
  • Multi-level subtotal rows excluded: the Check-in and Baggage reports carry rows marked as totals at six levels — cabin class, flight, segment, route, region and TC area — and adding them up directly would multiply passenger counts sixfold. This report uses only the detail rows with cabin class F, J, W, Y or C, and validates them back against the total rows.
  • Month assignment = creation month: this is consistent with the WorldTracer monthly report and with existing Airport Operations Div. practice, and because a case's month never changes once it is created, the monthly series of case counts and mishandled baggage rates cannot be contaminated by closure progress. The denominator (traffic) must, however, be counted on a flight month basis, and roughly 2.1–3.0% of cases each month relate to a flight in another month (about 30 cases in Jan, 37 in Feb, 41 in Mar, 24 in Apr, 26 in May, 28 in Jun and 30 in Jul). Because inflow and outflow are of similar size each month and offset one another, the direction of the trend is unaffected; only the absolute level of an individual month is.
  • Departure Station assignment rule: the first JX flight in the case itinerary that can be matched to the P31 flight table is taken, and the origin of that flight's segment is used as the Departure Station. Flight numbers are first normalised by removing spaces and leading zeros (JX 0002 → JX2), and where one flight number maps to several segments the one with the largest passenger count is taken (only 5 flight numbers in the period, all diversions or alternate landings). Of the 8,576 cases in the period, 98.6% (8,452 cases) resolve; the 124 unresolved cases are excluded from every station rate and therefore inflate no station. For damage cases, 6,550 of 6,595 = 99.3% can be assigned to a Segment.
  • Other-carrier liability separated out: 645 RL 54 cases (bag not received from another carrier) and 31 RL 77 cases (other-carrier handling error), 676 cases in total, are excluded from every station rate and route rate and are shown instead under interline transfer failure in Section 01 and in the partner ranking in Section 15, so that another carrier's problem is not counted against a JX station.
  • Currency conversion: the company's official monthly exchange rates (1,114 records, JAN26–JUL26) are applied to each case according to its "creation month" and converted to TWD. Total compensation for the period is TWD 7,941,425, and the six compensation categories sum to that total. Amount strings have been handled in all their formats (TWD 500, VND1239300, NO FEE, INSURANCE, "-", and comma-separated multi-currency strings such as USD 46, TWD 250, which are converted separately and then added). No currency was left without an exchange rate.
  • RL code classification follows the official reference table: the case file now includes a _Reference sheet (the official IATA / WorldTracer table of 60 codes), and every code appearing in this period has been checked one by one against the classification mapping, with no code left unclassified. A safeguard has also been added to the code: if a code that has not appeared before shows up in future (such as the pilferage variants 93/95/96/98, loading error 31, or the tagging codes 11/17), it is assigned by the tens digit of its major category and raises a warning, rather than being placed silently under Other.
  • The damage share has two bases (this is asked every period): the 76.9% damage share on the KPI card is the number of cases on the damage sheet divided by all cases (6,595 / 8,576); the 76.6% damage figure in the summary and in How to read this is damage cases classified by RL code (6,569 cases), alongside 25 pilfered cases (0.3%) and 1,982 delayed cases (23.1%). The difference arises because one case on the damage sheet carries RL 79 (report raised in error) and is classified as delayed. Both are correct; the bases differ.
  • August data fully excluded: the case file contains 443 cases from August 2026, but the four other source categories — traffic, check-in, loading and exchange rates — all stop at July, and August was only one third complete (extract date 8 August, August closure rate 79.2%), so no ratio can be formed and the month is removed in full. One outlier case from December 2025 was also filtered out.
  • Data maturity (affects amounts, not case counts): monthly closure rates are 99.8% for Jan, 99.8% for Feb, 99.5% for Mar, 98.9% for Apr, 97.7% for May, 97.2% for Jun and 88.8% for Jul. Compensation is booked only on closure, so the July amount is necessarily understated; Sections 05 and 06 mark it with muted shading and a hollow data point. The fall at the end of the compensation series must not be read as compensation decreasing.
  • Cases are entered retrospectively: Jan–Jun shows 7,438 cases this period against 7,414 for the same period in the previous edition, 24 more (+0.3%), being cases that entered the system between the two extracts. Recent months may therefore still be revised slightly upward, by an order of about 0.3%, which does not affect how the trend is read.
  • Section 20 uses system estimates: baggage loading intensity by cabin class comes from the EST (estimated) field in P33, not from item-by-item weighing. Its bag count (3,724,382 bags) and the actual P31 bag count used in Sections 01 and 02 (3,800,680 bags) come from different sources and differ by about 2%; the two must not be substituted for one another or added together.
  • Checked-in passengers and carried passengers are not the same: the Check-in report shows 3,591,919 checked-in passengers for the period, 35,499 more than the 3,556,420 passengers carried in P31 (+1.0%), which is a definitional difference between check-in and actual carriage (it includes passengers who did not board). Section 23 uses the Check-in report's own total as its denominator and does not mix it with Section 01.
  • The channel classification in Section 23 is not yet confirmed: the source file provides only six channel codes with no definitions, and the data contains no separate agent-assisted counter field (the six together already cover 98.8% of passengers). The share of each individual channel is therefore reliable, but the self-service total depends on how the codes are defined; the classification used in this report is stated explicitly in that section and flagged as to be verified. MOB mobile check-in is also zero for the whole period and ACI appears only from June; both have been raised with the system owners under action item 7.
  • Section 21 (SBD) and Section 22 (O&D) are new this period: SBD comes from the self bag drop fields of the Baggage report and is assigned to the departure station; its total (3,798,234 bags) differs from the P31 bag count (3,800,680 bags) by 2,446 bags (0.06%), which is a difference in report cut-off. An important limitation when reading SBD: of the 34 stations meeting the checked-baggage threshold, 27 recorded zero self bag drop in the period (including Tokyo Narita and all five U.S. stations); this means equipment not installed or not activated, not passengers declining to adopt it, so the station adoption ranking is in substance a ranking of equipment coverage. The report distinguishes the two explicitly in that section and in insight 7, so that an equipment issue is not misread as a passenger behaviour issue. O&D resolves 3,302,546 passengers, 92.9% of P31 carried traffic, with the remainder marked UNKNOWN in the source file and unmatchable; this file contains no excess baggage amount field, so excess baggage still cannot be attributed at passenger level.
  • Correlation is not causation: transfer passenger share against the delayed-baggage departure rate gives r = +0.80, and group passenger share against the departure mishandled baggage rate gives r = −0.34; both are cross-sectional correlations at station level (n = 34 stations). The U.S. hubs combine transfer intensity and long-haul heavy loading, and the two cannot be separated with the available data; the negative correlation for group passengers is largely a proxy for route character (group traffic concentrates on leisure point-to-point routes).
  • Closure timeliness is measured to the day: the source data carries no timestamps, so every average Days to Close is computed in calendar days; and cases not yet closed are excluded from the average, so recent months read low (the slow ones have not entered yet).
  • Historical months move slightly each time the report is rerun: this report recomputes everything from the latest source files every period rather than freezing a snapshot of the months already delivered. The case count, compensation amount and cause distribution for a given month may therefore differ slightly in the next edition — the sources are late documentation, RL code corrections and subsequent closures, which are natural revisions of the data itself and not a change of method. Days to Close is the most affected: the older a month is, the more it is revised upward as difficult cases close. When comparing across periods, always use the figures from the latest edition.
  • Conclusions the data cannot support are deliberately not drawn: although the decline in the mishandled baggage rate this period has been confirmed by three tests, there was no corresponding improvement measure and seven months cannot separate seasonality, so the report does not record it as an operational result and handles it as a to-be-verified list instead (see insight 1). Section 01 likewise does not claim that this network outperforms the industry benchmark, because both the numerator definition and the completeness of delayed-baggage capture differ from SITA.
